From: Lila Park <lila@halcyon.ai>

Cc: support@halcyon.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Halcyon trial - streaming behavior under load

Hi Marcus / Grace,

We're seeing repeated stalls in streaming responses while running our integration load tests this morning. The problem is most visible when we push concurrent sessions to ~150 connections: after a few minutes token emission pauses for 3-8s intermittently, then resumes. On our side this looks like chunked frames are arriving in bursts and sometimes a timeout is thrown client-side (WebSocket close code 1006).

I attached a session trace and a short log capture from the client (session-trace-20270914.json, client-headers.txt). We tried increasing the keepalive frequency and it reduced the frequency of stalls but didn't remove them. This is blocking tomorrow's product demo.

Can you confirm whether this is a customer-tenant issue or something on Redwood's serving plane? If you need a full pcap we can collect that but wanted to start here.

Thanks,
Lila Park
Sr. Platform Engineer, Halcyon.ai

Hi Lila — thanks for the traces and the clear reproduction steps. We're sorry this is impacting your demo.

Immediate plan:
- I've asked David (SRE) and Jonas (runtime) to start triage.
- Can your team confirm the exact client SDK version and whether the traffic was routed through any proxy/load balancer on your side? (I saw some unusual headers in client-headers.txt.)
- We'll set up a 30m troubleshooting call in the next hour; Marcus will send the Zoom link.

Temporary mitigation we can push quickly: if this is a server-side chunk coalescing/timeout issue we can flip a config on your tenant to reduce continuous batching and increase token emission flush frequency. This typically trades some throughput efficiency for smoother per-token delivery. If you want us to try that now, say the word and we'll apply it to the trial tenant and monitor.

I appreciate the urgency — we should be able to have an initial root-cause hypothesis within a few hours.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Halcyon trial - streaming behavior under load

Quick findings from the first pass on the traces Lila sent:
- We see a pattern where the server's chunked transfer encoder buffers ~20-40ms worth of tokens but then pauses for multiple seconds under high concurrency; pauses correlate with increased CPU steal on one of the inference hosts (i-rt-32) and a burst of GC activity in the request router process.
- WebSocket frames are not being explicitly closed by the server; the client-side 1006 closes are consistent with network-level inactivity/timeouts.
- Client headers show a nonstandard keepalive interval (15s) — our default expects ~30s. That could change how we treat idle detection in proxies.

Action items:
1) Jonas: capture runtime metrics from i-rt-32 for the affected window and check kernel-sched stats; prioritize any hot kernel tasks.
2) Ops: temporarily pin Halcyon trial traffic to a dedicated small pool (avoid noisy neighbor) and flip the continuous-batching -> aggressive-flush config for that pool.
3) Marcus: coordinate an ASAP deploy of a probe that logs chunk-emit timestamps for correlation.

I'll keep the ticket updated. If we confirm CPU scheduling pressure is the trigger we'll want to either move the pool to a different instance family or adjust the router process niceness.

-David
David Kim
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Persistent streaming stalls during high-concurrency window — Halcyon (trial)

Lila — quick update and recommended next steps after two triage iterations: 

What we confirmed:
- Root cause: intermittent CPU scheduling pressure on one inference host in the pool combined with upstream proxy idle-detection mismatch caused chunk emission to pause, which clients interpreted as a dead connection (1006).
- Remediation applied: we pinned your trial traffic to a dedicated 3-node pool (no noisy neighbors) and enabled aggressive-flush (reduces continuous-batching window). Early telemetry shows the per-token gap median dropped from ~1.8s to 40ms under the same concurrency.

Planned follow-ups:
- Jonas will land a small router fix (INF-7193) to track chunk-emit timestamps (merge request open; see Drive link).
- Ops will schedule a capacity-family migration for that pool next week to avoid recurrence under heavier burst profiles.
- Commercial: Neha will coordinate a goodwill credit if any residual instability persists during the next scheduled demo.

If you're comfortable, we'll keep the dedicated pool for the trial until your demo window completes; otherwise we can revert once the trial ends. Appreciate the patience — please let me know if you'd like an exec-level briefing before the demo.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
